answer_summary: Ranking of Red/Ad combinations by decreasing NH3 yield: B > C > D > A. Grounding: at fixed acid (A vs C, pKa 13.7) the stronger reductant Cp2V (E°=-1.10 V) beats Cp2Ni (-0.09 V), so C > A; at fixed reductant (Cp2V) the higher-pKa acid wins, so B (pKa 15.0) > C (13.7) > D (10.6). The cross-parameter pair D vs A is settled by the Bordwell CPET conversion 0.0591 V/pKa: D's reductant advantage (1.01 V) exceeds its acid disadvantage (3.1 x 0.0591 = 0.183 V) by >5x, so D > A. Final: B > C > D > A.
assumptions: YieldOrder.potential_mono: at fixed pKa, a more negative reductant E° gives higher NH3 yield (grounded in the problem's printed reference yields 1 vs 3 on T7_page-3.png: Cp2Cr 0 mol vs Cp2Co 9.1 mol at near-equal pKa).

YieldOrder.pKa_mono: at fixed reductant, a higher-pKa CF3SO3- acid gives higher NH3 yield (grounded in the printed reference yields 3 vs 4: pKa 13.9 -> 9.1 mol vs pKa 14.4 -> 11.8 mol, same Cp2Co reductant and counterion).

YieldOrder.bordwell_joint: Bordwell linear free-energy relation for CPET with conversion 0.0591 V per pKa unit at 298 K (trusted general physical-organic chemistry law); used only to compare D vs A, where both E° and pKa change.
